topic: 5 hand impedance: fingertip pad tangential stiffness and damping
citation: Wiertlewski M, Hayward V (2012) Mechanical behavior of the fingertip in the range of frequencies and displacements relevant to touch. J Biomech 45(11):1869-1874
task_or_setup: High-mobility probe (stiffness <= 1.2 N/m, damping <= 0.5 N s/m) drives a flat plate tangentially under the index fingertip; frequency sweeps; normal force held 0.25-2 N; Kelvin-Voigt / mass-spring-damper fit
comparator: Nakazawa et al. 2000 and Pataky et al. 2005 (cited values); medial-lateral vs proximal-distal
key_quantitative_findings: Tangential stiffness 0.6-2.0 kN/m, damping 0.75-2.38 N s/m, entrained mass 110-230 mg at 0.5 N normal force (Table 1: medial-lateral k 0.59-1.67 N/mm, b 0.80-2.38 N s/m; proximal-distal k 0.71-2.08 N/mm). Power laws in normal force n (N): k = 1.48 n^0.35 N/mm, b = 1.78 n^0.35 N s/m (Table 2). Elastic up to about 100 Hz, viscous above; parameters drift upward about 0.5 %/s when loaded.
units_and_conditions: N/m, N s/m, g; normal force 0.25-2 N; small tangential amplitudes
locator: Author's copy p. 1 (introduction), Table 1 (p. 4), Table 2 (p. 4), Sec. 5 (p. 5)
limitations: Single fingertip on a flat plate, not a tripod grasp of a round barrel; excludes the finger joints, which dominate the tip-referred grip compliance
relevance_to_design: Upper bound on the stiffness of one grip contact: three pads in shear give about 4-5 kN/m at 1 N each, eight times the tip-referred HAP-26 grasp stiffness (575 N/m)
transferability_reason: Same tissue and force range as a light pen grip; the contact geometry and joint compliance differ
design_implication: The pen-grip compliance is set by the finger joints, not the skin; the split between translational and rotational grip compliance cannot be derived from pad data and must be measured (EXP-I01)
search_query: WebSearch: Wiertlewski Hayward mechanical behavior of the fingertip range of frequencies; curl https://cim.mcgill.ca/~haptic/pub/MW-VH-JBM-12.pdf

citation: Formica D, Charles SK, Zollo L, Guglielmelli E, Hogan N, Krebs HI (2012) The passive stiffness of the wrist and forearm. J Neurophysiol 108(4):1158-1166
task_or_setup: Wrist and forearm rehabilitation robot; relaxed subjects; 1-D protocol (FE, RUD, PS) and 2-D protocol (FE-RUD combinations); linearised stiffness matrices
key_quantitative_findings: 1-D: toward flexion 0.554 +/- 0.170, toward extension 1.021 N m/rad (mean). 2-D mean symmetric stiffness matrix [1.28 -0.18; -0.18 1.74] +/- [0.42 0.08; 0.08 0.34] N m/rad (FE, RUD); eigenvalues 1.80 and 1.22 N m/rad; ellipse rotated about 20 deg from the anatomical axes. Pronation/supination 0.2-0.3 N m/rad. Prior studies <0.15 to 3 N m/rad.
units_and_conditions: N m/rad; relaxed muscles, small displacements
limitations: Passive (relaxed) wrist; writing with a grip co-contracts and stiffens it; no inertia or damping
relevance_to_design: Sets the order of magnitude of the rotational restraint behind the grip for the torque-device (gyroscope/CMG) hand calculation
transferability_reason: Wrist joint is the same; active writing posture stiffer than relaxed
design_implication: A pen-mounted torque device fights at least 1-2 N m/rad of wrist stiffness plus hand inertia (about 7 N m/rad at 8 Hz for 3e-3 kg m^2) if it tries to steady the hand; its mN m torques move the hand by fractions of a milliradian

topic: 7 tremor biomechanics: distribution of essential tremor among upper-limb degrees of freedom
citation: Pigg AC, Thompson-Westra J, Mente K, Maurer CW, Haubenberger D, Hallett M, Charles SK (2020) Distribution of tremor among the major degrees of freedom of the upper limb in subjects with Essential Tremor. Clin Neurophysiol 131(11):2700-2712
task_or_setup: Upper-limb motion capture during postural and kinetic tasks in several limb configurations; tremor distribution over 7 DOF shoulder to wrist
comparator: Postural vs kinetic tasks; configurations; subject characteristics
key_quantitative_findings: Kinetic tremor greatest in forearm pronation-supination and wrist flexion-extension, intermediate in shoulder internal-external rotation and wrist radial-ulnar deviation, then shoulder and elbow flexion-extension, least in shoulder abduction-adduction; postural tremor similar except a smaller pronation-supination share; distribution consistent over repetitions (abstract; numeric amplitudes not accessed).
limitations: Abstract only; no pen grasp or writing; amplitudes not extracted
relevance_to_design: Supports modelling a rotational (wrist) tremor component, the only component a pen-mounted gyroscopic device can sense directly
transferability_reason: Same patient group; writing posture and grasp not studied
design_implication: Simulate tremor as hand-path translation plus a wrist rotation about a pivot 150-200 mm behind the grip; measure the split on writers (EXP-I02)
search_query: Europe PMC TITLE:"Distribution of tremor among the major degrees of freedom of the upper limb"

topic: 7 tremor biomechanics: wrist rotation dynamics dominated by stiffness
citation: Charles SK, Hogan N (2011) Dynamics of wrist rotations. J Biomech 44(4):614-621
task_or_setup: Model of FE and RUD wrist rotations with inertia, damping and stiffness (stiffness measured, inertia and damping from literature) driven by measured kinematics of +/-15 deg movements
key_quantitative_findings: Passive stiffness is the major impedance for wrist rotations; inertia and passive damping matter only for very fast movements; inertial interaction torques negligible; stiffness and damping interaction torques significant (abstract; parameter values not accessed).
limitations: Abstract only; healthy subjects; movements, not tremor
relevance_to_design: Frames the hand-rotation hand calculation (stiffness + inertia at 4-12 Hz)
transferability_reason: No numbers extracted; tremor frequencies are above the movement speeds studied
design_implication: Treat the hand's rotational impedance as an assumption (inertia 2-4.5e-3 kg m^2 plus HAP-32 stiffness) in any torque-device estimate
search_query: Europe PMC TITLE:"Dynamics of wrist rotations"

topic: Passive tuned vibration absorber worn on the forearm (Vib-bracelet)
citation: Buki E, Katz R, Zacksenhouse M, Schlesinger I (2018) Vib-bracelet: a passive absorber for attenuating forearm tremor. Med Biol Eng Comput 56:923-930
task_or_setup: Dynamic vibration absorber tuned to the tremor frequency for pronation-supination tremor; prototypes on a mechanical forearm model; simulations
key_quantitative_findings: Attenuation in the 4-6 Hz range with a maximum amplitude attenuation of 85 % (abstract).
units_and_conditions: Amplitude attenuation on a mechanical model, 4-6 Hz
limitations: Mechanical model; tuned narrow band; absorber mass not in the abstract
relevance_to_design: Tuned absorbers work on a resonant limb segment with a large moving mass; the pen is not resonant in the tremor band
transferability_reason: Different structure (forearm rotation) and mass scale
design_implication: A cap tuned-mass damper cannot reproduce this: the pen's grip mode is at 30-60 Hz and the absorber stroke is about 1 mm

topic: Active stabilised spoon (Gyenno) in Parkinson's disease: pilot with no benefit
citation: Ryden LE, Matar E, Szeto JYY, Hammond DA, Clouston P, Lewis SJG (2020) Shaken not stirred: a pilot study testing a gyroscopic spoon stabilization device in Parkinson's disease and tremor. Ann Indian Acad Neurol 23(3):409-411
task_or_setup: Rice transfers between bowls 50 cm apart with the device on and off (blinded to state): 60 s timed task and 3-attempt task
participants_or_bench: 10 PD patients recruited, 8 analysed (mostly rest and low-amplitude postural tremor)
key_quantitative_findings: 60 s task: less rice with the device on (difference -22.81 to -3.39 g 95 % CI, p = 0.014); 3-attempt task: no significant difference in grams (p = 0.200) or time (p = 0.703).
limitations: Very small, on-medication, mostly rest tremor; single session
relevance_to_design: Active handheld stabilisation does not help every tremor phenotype; benefit depends on tremor type during the task
transferability_reason: Same patient group; eating task, not writing
design_implication: Pre-register tremor phenotype and task tremor amplitude as covariates in pen trials
